purpose: Editorial review of historical event descriptions. This file is not imported by the application and does not create calendar events.
date_semantics: start_date and end_date are inclusive event dates. Unknown dates and times remain null. Google Calendar's exclusive all-day end is a later import conversion, not this source format.
usage: Use description for the full website copy and calendar_description for a concise calendar summary with speakers and public resources. Collections summarize child events and must not create duplicate calendar events. Programs need a deliberate multiweek representation. Every record remains a draft pending review.

evidence_statuses.day_of_evidence: A day-of announcement or reminder was located; completion is not independently confirmed.
evidence_statuses.live_event_evidence: Contemporaneous activity supports the event being underway.
evidence_statuses.past_event_listing: An event platform lists this past event; completion is not independently confirmed.
evidence_statuses.announcement_only: Announced or scheduled; actual occurrence needs confirmation.
evidence_statuses.partially_confirmed: Part of the program is confirmed; another portion remains scheduled-only.

events.title: Phillip Christoffersen: Beyond Guardrails
events.description: Phillip Christoffersen, a PhD researcher in MIT CSAIL's Algorithmic Alignment Group, presented Beyond Guardrails: Towards a Common Specification Language for AI Agent Domains. The talk examined why existing guardrails often constrain outcomes rather than processes and introduced a specification language for describing agent environments and safety requirements. It explored generating training data for safety-constrained policies and using coding agents to make specification more scalable, with implications for oversight of language-model agents.

events.title: Andreea Bobu: Four Pillars of Human-Aligned AI Representations
events.description: Andreea Bobu, an MIT AeroAstro and CSAIL professor who leads the CLEAR Lab, presented a framework for AI systems that understand the concepts people care about. Four Pillars of Human-Aligned AI Representations focused on completeness, minimality, efficiency, and interpretability. Drawing on robot learning, the talk examined generating concepts as code with language models and using language-guided abstractions to ignore irrelevant information, connecting these methods to meaningful human oversight.

events.title: MAIA Technical Governance Competition
events.location: MIT, Cambridge, MA; multiweek competition. Scheduled workshops at MIT Room 3-333.
events.description:
MAIA's Technical Governance Competition brought students together to turn technical knowledge of AI into practical policy proposals. Over several weeks, participants developed a concise policy artifact and supporting report explaining how their proposal would work, how it could be enforced, and why it was technically sound. The competition offered a $10,000 prize pool and encouraged concrete ideas such as improvements to existing legislation, auditing requirements, and rules for AI deployment.

Winning projects addressed three different governance problems: transparency and grid stewardship for AI data centers in Maine; financial responsibility and insurance for advanced AI systems; and liability for autonomous code generation and deployment. The competition was organized by Anooshka Pendyal and Neha Muramalla, with Ionel Chiosa also listed on the organizing team. Judge Paulo Carvão later wrote about the competition and its proposals in Forbes.

events.description: Riya Tyagi planned a hands-on session on emergent misalignment, where training a model on narrowly problematic data can lead to broader changes in behavior. events.title: AISF Hackathon
events.description: AISF fellows spent a full day turning ideas from the fellowship into hands-on AI safety projects, with team formation, mentorship, meals, and evening presentations. Documented projects included adding a small learned module to a language model to resist jailbreaks, using Petri to compare lying and reward hacking under ordinary versus competitive task settings, and building an agent to demonstrate manipulative persuasion. Teams presented their work at the end of the day and participants voted on projects.

events.title: Mission Strawberry: Fool the Language Model
events.description: MAIA members and AISF fellows competed to devise questions that people could solve but leading language models would get wrong. Mission Strawberry put human teams up against GPT-5-Thinking and Gemini 3 in a playful test of model reasoning, with food and strawberry-themed treats. The organizer's post-event recap highlighted four submissions that fooled both models while every human team found the correct answer.

additional_candidates.description: Zac Hatfield-Dodds of Anthropic led a practical mini-workshop for MAIA and AISST members on contributing to open-source projects. additional_candidates.title: Causal Interventions for Interpretability: IAP Workshop
additional_candidates.description: A two-week, not-for-credit IAP workshop supported by MIT AI Alignment introducing causal methods for interpreting neural networks. The January 23–27 lecture week covered causal mediation analysis, induction heads and in-context learning, toy models and algorithmic tasks, probing language models, and broader perspectives on interpretability, with optional hands-on notebook sessions. A following project week was scheduled for January 30–February 3.
